title: Improve the way you name/rename a hostpot
line: With a long login name, the default hotspot name is now shortened to fit Wi-Fi's 32-byte limit, so turning on the hotspot no longer fails.
explanation: Configuration::hotspotName() defaults to the login name plus "-hotspot" with no length check. An SSID may be at most 32 bytes, so with a login name of 25 bytes or more NetworkManager rejects the connection ("802-11-wireless.ssid: SSID length is out of range <1-32> bytes") and the Hotspot button fails, as in the report. The change chops characters off the login name until the whole default name fits in 32 UTF-8 bytes; a name the user set in the configuration is left untouched.

commits.message:
libs/editor: keep the default hotspot name within 32 bytes

The default hotspot name is the login name followed by "-hotspot", so with
a long login name it went over the 32 bytes allowed for an SSID and turning
on the hotspot failed. Now the login name is shortened until it fits.

BUG: 527192

media.caption: Wi-Fi KCM > Configure with login name beedell.roke_julian_lockhart (the reporter's): default hotspot name beedell.roke_julian_lockhart-hotspot is 37 bytes
Same with the fix: beedell.roke_julian_lock-hotspot, exactly 32 bytes

review.text: Fixes the real failure (default SSID login-name + '-hotspot' exceeding NetworkManager's 32-byte limit) at the single place the default is built, leaving user-set names untouched. Verified with the reporter's login name via a shim and nmcli's own validation. Minor: chop(1) works on UTF-16 units, so a non-BMP character at the cut could be split, but that is a negligible edge case.
